checks.label: Ohm's law stipulates that the voltage drop across and current through a resistor are related by V = IR: on every V = IR screen the volts are the amps × the ohms
They all are combinations of just two equations, Ohm's law and power: P = I²R gives the same watts as V = IR followed by P = VI, on every P = I²R screen and on the 2.3 kW heater
P = I × R × I, which is the same as I × I × R, which is the same as I²R
Form linear equations consistent with data provided: each job's equation is built from its own amounts, and its answer gives them back

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, and every wrong answer offered is the one a named slip gives, its check failing or its order wrong: a step done again instead of undone; a division the wrong way round; milliamps put in as amps; a current doubled instead of squared; I × R squared; the square left out; a fixed amount added instead of taken off; the rate and the fixed amount swapped; what is left taken off instead of added, its equation's answer failing the job's check; or milliamps turned into amps one place too far

Every picture, finished, puts each amount under its letter in that letter's unit and ends on the check: the steps done to the unknown with the undo under them, last step first, or, where P is the unknown, the steps worked forwards with the check by V = IR and P = VI; the P = I²R screen shows P = VI turned into I × I × R; a wrong answer's check, order or equation is in the warning colour, inside the picture
Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture shows the answer

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion within 2.5 s and a slip within 1 s; parts start at least 0.45 s apart
